title: Development of Budget Management System Using Visual Basic .NET and MySQL Database: A Desktop Application for Personal Financial Tracking
tldr: A desktop budget management system using Visual Basic .NET and MySQL was developed to provide offline, privacy-focused personal financial tracking with automated income/expense summaries and balance calculation.
problem_and_motivation: Many individuals lack reliable, accessible tools for consistent financial discipline, while existing manual methods and cloud-based alternatives suffer from errors, privacy risks, or connectivity dependencies. There is a need for a simple, secure, offline, and cost-free personal finance application that provides real-time financial insights and promotes financial literacy.
approach: The system was developed using a developmental research design following the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) framework with six stages: planning, analysis, design, implementation, testing, and deployment.
A two-tier client-server architecture separates the presentation layer (Visual Basic .NET) from the data layer (MySQL) for modularity and maintainability.
The MySQL database db_budget contains a transactions table with fields for transaction_id, amount, remarks, transaction_type, and transaction_date.
The Visual Basic .NET interface provides an input panel, action toolbar with CRUD operations, a DataGridView for transaction display, and a summary panel for real-time financial totals.
Parameterized SQL queries are used for all database operations to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities.
Date-based filtering enables users to analyze financial data within specific timeframes.
Performance testing confirmed that operations remained responsive with databases containing up to 5,000 entries.
The system operates entirely offline after initial database configuration, eliminating dependency on internet connectivity.
findings: num: Transaction insertion, modification, and deletion were completed in under 0.5 seconds.
num: Data retrieval and aggregation queries remained responsive at under 1 second for databases containing up to 5,000 entries.
Unit and integration tests confirmed accurate interaction between the Visual Basic .NET interface and MySQL database.
Functional testing validated all user-facing features including recording, viewing, filtering, updating, and summarizing transactions.
Usability testing with participants of diverse technical backgrounds confirmed the interface was intuitive and accessible with minimal guidance required.
Color-coded visual indicators (green for surplus, red for deficit) provide immediate feedback on financial status.
The system maintains complete user privacy by storing all financial records locally without cloud dependency.
Open-source design enables transparency, customizability, and educational value for students and novice developers.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: The paper contributes a practical, open-source desktop application that demonstrates the integration of Visual Basic .NET and MySQL for personal financial management. It provides an offline, privacy-preserving alternative to commercial cloud-based tools. The system serves as an educational model for students learning database-driven software development. The work validates that accessible, simple technology can effectively support personal financial literacy and independence. It identifies clear directions for future enhancement including installation automation, cross-platform support, and advanced visualization.
directly_justifies: Simple, well-structured desktop applications can effectively support individual financial literacy.
Local data storage provides users full control over their financial information.
Offline capability eliminates reliance on internet connectivity and recurring costs.
The system occupies a unique niche between basic spreadsheets and complex commercial software.
limits: The database configuration process requires manual setup through XAMPP and phpMyAdmin, which may challenge non-technical users.
The application depends on Windows, restricting cross-platform deployment.
The single-user design limits shared budgeting scenarios such as household or group use.
Data backup must be performed manually, creating potential risks of data loss.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains was performed. The paper was flagged as relevant to domains 3.A (Expense Categorization Frameworks), 4.A (Landscape of Existing Personal Finance Systems), 9.A (Mobile-First Design), 9.B (Mobile UX), 9.C (Offline-First Architecture), 10.A (Data Privacy), 10.B (User Trust), and 13.A (Savings Goal Management). Domains 1.A-1.C (Filipino Young Professionals) were considered and rejected because the paper does not focus on any specific demographic. Domains 2.A-2.D (Culturally Specific Practices, Seasonal Spending) were rejected as the paper does not address cultural or seasonal patterns. Domains 3.B-3.C (Category Design, Allocation Constraints) were rejected for lacking discussion of category design principles. Domains 4.B (Limitations and Gaps) was considered and rejected due to no systematic gap analysis. Domains 5.A-7.E (Behavioral Profiles, Predictive Modeling, Budgeting Strategies) were rejected as the paper does not address these algorithmic or modeling approaches. Domains 8.A-8.C (Anomaly Detection) were rejected for no anomaly detection. Domains 10.C (Consent Management) was rejected for no data portability discussion. Domains 11.A-14.C were rejected for no engagement, evaluation, debt management, synthetic data, or ML deployment. Overall topical coverage is focused on desktop application development, offline operation, and privacy preservation.

limitations: Manual installation process requiring MySQL configuration via XAMPP presents barriers for non-technical users. [unacknowledged]
Single-user design restricts collaborative and household budgeting scenarios. [unacknowledged]
Windows-only dependency limits cross-platform compatibility for macOS, Linux, and mobile users. [unacknowledged]
Manual backup requirement creates data loss risks if users fail to perform regular backups. [unacknowledged]
Lack of automated setup, expense categorization, graphical reporting, and recurring transaction features. [unacknowledged]
remember_this: The system is a desktop-based offline personal finance application built with Visual Basic .NET and MySQL.
All financial data is stored locally, providing complete user control and privacy without cloud dependency.
The system dynamically calculates total income, total expenses, and current balance with color-coded visual indicators.
Performance testing confirmed query responsiveness under 1 second for databases with up to 5,000 entries.
The system prioritizes simplicity, accessibility, and educational value over complex commercial features.
